clue.text: Old-fashioned Margaret may be hard to fit in

parts.note: square is slang for conventional or out of date
Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned woman called Margaret might struggle to fit into modern company.
explanation.walkthrough: A square peg in a round hole is the stock image of something or someone that does not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a misfit, a person or thing that cannot be accommodated by its surroundings.

clue.text: St Bernard fabulously -unkempt ?

parts.note: a big, hairy breed of hound, with fabulously hinting at a long rambling tale with a pointless ending

explanation.walkthrough: A St Bernard is literally a hairy hound, and the word 'fabulously' points to the long, pointless joke known by the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-haired hound, and the term for a rambling story with an anticlimactic punchline.

clue.text: Improper description of bill not yet payable

definitions.text: description of bill not yet payable
definitions.meaning: a bill not yet owing is not due

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: unwarranted or excessive, and literally not yet owed, as a bill before its settlement date.

clue.text: Carmen's accommodation in Rye perhaps, from a distance

indicators.note: in places the lodging inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests one possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: read as car-men, motorists, whose lodging is a motel

explanation.surface: The opera's Carmen lodges in a Sussex town, observed from afar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' is not the opera heroine but car-men, drivers, who stay at a motel. 'perhaps' makes REY of the town's name. Rye is a small town in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at a distance, without being physically present.

clue.text: Press leader and articles on the Temple

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an and the are the indefinite and definite articles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial and some features on a famous building in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' and 'leader' suggest a newspaper editorial, but only P is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The domed temple in Rome built for all the gods is the best-known building of the name.

clue.text: Foundation of-golf's beginning-eighteen holes:

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a full round of golf is eighteen holes

explanation.surface: The basics of golf: start at the beginning and play all eighteen holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A base or groundwork on which something is built.

clue.text: A Greek letter's signifying a point in orbit

parts.note: psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet; with the 's it gives an extra S

explanation.surface: A letter of the Greek alphabet stands for a particular place along an orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signifying' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy the term names either extreme point of an elliptical orbit, nearest to or furthest from the body orbited.

clue.text: Marbles associated with skittles

definitions.meaning: an alley, or ally, is a type of large playing marble
skittles is played down a long lane

explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is the British game of ninepins.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: playing marbles called allies, and the lanes on which skittles or ninepins are bowled.

clue.text: Raining so badly in Italy -give it a miss

indicators.note: badly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wet weather in Italy, so skip the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give it a miss' sounds like advice to skip the trip, but it means 'call it a Miss': the Italian word for an unmarried young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian form of address for an unmarried young woman, equivalent to the English title Miss.

clue.text: Try to find about fifty with glossy coats

indicators.note: about means the search word goes around the numeral

parts.note: to seek is to try to find
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Searching for some fifty animals with shiny fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth and shiny, as the coat of a well-groomed animal.

clue.text: Terribly bad sign for the inner man

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A very bad portent for someone's insides, perhaps an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' turns BAD into ABD.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is a humorous phrase for the stomach or belly, the seat of appetite.

clue.text: Noble Heart-one horse to whom one is bound

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the letters inside the first and last are taken

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
gee, or gee-gee, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A noble steed called Heart is the beneficiary of a binding promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of NOBLE is OBL, its letters without the first and last.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this is the person to whom another owes a duty under a bond or contract.

clue.text: Like Alfred, King George has to take food

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
to eat is to take food

explanation.surface: Like a famous king, a later monarch must stop to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred, the ninth-century king of Wessex, is the only English king called 'the Great'.
explanation.definitionFit: King Alfred is known by the epithet attached to his name, so one like him shares that title.

clue.text: Motor-horn sound precedes Keystone antics. See omission? Tinny piano

indicators.note: precedes places the horn's sound before what follows

parts.note: a car horn goes honk

indicators.note: antics are capers, so the letters left over caper about into a new order
omission says the letters of the word before it are left out of the jumbled word

explanation.surface: A slapstick silent film with honking horns and Keystone Cops chaos, to a cheap piano accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See omission' takes S, E, E out of KEYSTONE, and 'antics' rearranges what is left, KYTON, as YTONK. The Keystone Cops were slapstick silent-film policemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A honky-tonk piano is an upright with a jangly, tinny tone, the kind played in cheap bars.

clue.text: Bound to make trouble about card-game for old coin

indicators.note: about places the anagram around the card game
making trouble means stirring things up, so the letters are stirred

parts.note: loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to cause a fuss over a game of cards, for the sake of an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like the definition (obliged), but it is anagram fodder: 'to make trouble' turns it into DOUBN, and 'about' wraps that round the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gold piece of former times, the treasure of pirate stories.

clue.text: Foreigner in S Africa has tail twisted under the circumstances

indicators.note: circum- means around, so the circumstances signals one piece standing around another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An outsider in South Africa whose tail has been twisted, given the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the circumstances' looks like a stock phrase, but 'the circumstances' (circum = around) says the word under stands around ITLA, which 'twisted' makes of the animal's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afrikaans word for an outlander, applied to British settlers in the Boer republics.

clue.text: Inclination for bowls

definitions.meaning: a leaning or prejudice in one direction
in lawn bowls each ball is weighted so that it curves

explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls is a game played on a flat green with weighted balls that curve as they slow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a tendency to lean one way: a prejudice of mind, and the built-in swerve of a bowling ball.

clue.text: Product of Samson's strong (if dead) lion.

definitions.text: Product of Samson's strong (if dead) lion.

parts.words: Product of Samson's strong (if dead) lion
parts.note: in the Bible Samson found bees making honey in the carcass of a lion he had killed, and set a riddle about it

explanation.walkthrough: Samson's riddle in Judges is 'Out of the strong came forth' this; the strong one was the lion, dead but full of honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey from the carcass is the sugary taste Samson's riddle names.

clue.text: Be-furred visitor to Bucking ham Palace

definitions.text: Be-furred visitor to Bucking ham Palace

parts.words: Be-furred visitor to Bucking ham Palace
parts.note: the nursery rhyme animal that went to London to visit the Queen and frightened a mouse under her chair

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs: 'where have you been? I've been to London to visit the Queen.' The royal residence, Buckingham Palace, is split across a line in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The furry pet of the nursery rhyme who travels to London to see the Queen.

clue.text: Snake bones-and a warrior queen

parts.note: a boa is a constricting snake
bones is slang for dice, once carved from bone

explanation.surface: A snake, some bones, and a fierce queen of the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni queen who led a revolt against Roman Britain, now more often called Boudicca.

clue.text: Sounds like how you walk out of it

definitions.text: Sounds like how you walk out of it

indicators.note: sounds like says the word meant is heard as another

parts.note: your gait is your manner of walking

explanation.surface: A riddle about a word that is pronounced like your style of walking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a gate is something you walk out through.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is the hinged barrier you pass through when leaving a field or garden.

clue.text: A terrible fade-out for here-tics

indicators.note: terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful end awaiting those who dissented from church teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is A FADEOUT; read as a whole, the clue also describes the burning of condemned heretics.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese phrase, act of faith, named the Inquisition's public sentencing and burning of condemned heretics.

clue.text: For half a cent genuine rice for example

indicators.note: half a word is its first half, here the opening pair of letters

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: Rice going cheap at half a cent, the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is one of the grains grown as a staple food crop.

clue.text: Tanner's spree

definitions.meaning: a tanner was the old British sixpence, also called by this slang name; the 's is is

explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was the pre-decimal British sixpenny piece, which was also nicknamed a bender because it bent easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: old slang for the sixpenny coin, and a wild bout of drinking.

clue.text: "From this chasm, with —— turmoil seething" (Coleridge)

parts.note: a line of Kubla Khan with one word gone, the word describing the turmoil as never stopping

explanation.walkthrough: The full line of Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan is 'And from this chasm, with ceaseless turmoil seething'; the dash marks the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective means unending, describing the turmoil that never stops.

clue.text: Sorceress would be round about fifty

indicators.note: the sorceress would become round if put about fifty, so taking fifty from round leaves her name
this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs

parts.note: a circle is round
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An enchantress would turn rotund if she gained fifty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Place her name about L and it would be CIRCLE, the round shape; so CIRCLE without L gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's crew into swine.

clue.text: Coin of the French 17

parts.note: du is French for of the
17 down is a furry animal, a domestic cat

explanation.surface: A coin from France connected to a clue elsewhere in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 17 down, whose last three letters give CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold or silver piece formerly used in many European countries.

clue.text: Animal's one under-garment

indicators.note: under places one below the garment in this down clue

parts.note: a coat is a garment
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An animal's single item of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under-garment' reads as underwear, but 'under' places I beneath COAT in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon-like mammal of Central and South America with a long snout.

clue.text: Carrots (so called) most important in Moscow

parts.note: Moscow was the capital of the Soviet Reds
head means chief or most important

explanation.surface: A nickname for the leading person in the Russian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrots' is a teasing nickname for someone with ginger hair; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots is a schoolyard nickname given to a person with ginger hair.

clue.text: Bird needs help, we hear, with a hat ornament

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by sound, not spelling

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A bird must be helped along to become a decoration for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette or knot of ribbon worn on a hat as a badge.

clue.text: Left, right ! One is wrong, to sign on

indicators.note: if something is wrong it is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant calls the step and spots one recruit out of time, then signs up new ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges R and ONE into ENRO; the drill call 'Left' supplies the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: To register formally, such as joining a course or the armed forces.

clue.text: Castanet performer at the Colosseum ?

parts.note: split castanet as cast a net: a fighter in the Roman arena who threw a net

explanation.walkthrough: 'Castanet' looks like the Spanish clicking instrument, but read as 'cast a net' it describes a type of Roman gladiator who fought with net and trident.
explanation.definitionFit: This class of gladiator fought armed with a weighted net and a trident.
